samples.summary: Freeze snap only grows, so insert→delete round trips leave the frozen band permanently larger
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` (merging.ts:207-233) only ever *increases* `rows`/`cols`; it never shrinks back. In `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:278-288) it is applied after every shift. Concrete round trip with the diff's own fixture: frozenRows=3, merges {A3:{rs:3}}. `POST insert {row,index:1,count:1}` → boundary 3→4, merge A4:A6, snap → frozenRows=6. Immediately undoing with `POST delete {row,index:1,count:1}` → deletedInFrozen=min(1,6-1+1)=1 → frozenRows=5, merge back to A3:A5, snap finds no straddle (5 is already past row 5) → the tab is left with frozenRows=5 where it started at 3. The structural edit is reversible for cells and merges but not for the freeze pane, so an API client (or the editor doing insert-then-delete) silently accumulates frozen rows. The controller doc comment (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:54-62) acknowledges the boundary may grow but not that it never comes back.

samples.summary: Snap is applied unconditionally, so a shift that touches neither the boundary nor any merge can still move the freeze on a pre-existing straddling document
samples.evidence: The snap at worksheet-structure.ts:278 runs on every `applyWorksheetShift`, not only when the boundary or the merge map actually moved. Legacy documents can carry a straddling block into the new shape unrepaired — `migrateLegacyWorksheet` copies `merges: cloneMergeRecord(legacy.merges)` and `frozenRows: legacy.frozenRows ?? 0` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-shape-migration.ts:444-450) with no snap. For such a document, an insert/delete far below the frozen band (index > frozen, so the freeze block at lines 254-269 is skipped and the block does not move) will still jump `frozenRows` to the bottom of the stale block, changing view state the request never asked to change. The repair is defensible, but it is an unannounced state change on an unrelated edit.

samples.summary: Editor path now pays the O(n²)-ish merge rescan twice per structural edit
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` rescans the whole merge list and restarts the loop on each change (merging.ts:216-230). In the editor, `YorkieStore.shiftCells` → `applyWorksheetShift` now runs it against the document's merges (worksheet-structure.ts:278), and `Sheet.shiftCells` then runs the identical computation again against `this.merges` (sheet.ts:1418-1423). Both produce the same value, so this is redundant work on every row/column insert/delete on sheets with many merged blocks.

finding.summary: `POST insert`/`delete` still creates the straddling-merge state the new guards exist to prevent — the backend shift does not snap the freeze the way `Sheet.shiftCells` now does
finding.evidence: `applyShift` calls `applyWorksheetShift` only. `shiftWorksheetViewState` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:246-265) mirrors the *old* `Sheet.shiftCells` freeze adjustment but has no `snapFreezePastMerges` pass, while `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1415-1429) now snaps after shifting merges. So an API insert/delete that moves the boundary and the merge map independently can leave a block across the freeze — the exact 'one door into a state the editor cannot paint' the new `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` doc claims to close — and, combined with the previous finding, then 409s every subsequent move.

verdict.reason: The snap the finding says is missing exists in `shiftWorksheetViewState`. packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:271-288 calls `snapFreezePastMerges(ws.merges, ws.frozenRows ?? 0, ws.frozenCols ?? 0)` and writes both snapped counts back, with a comment explicitly naming the insert/delete path as "the one remaining door" it closes; the helper is imported at line 18. The reviewer's cited range (246-265) ends one line before this block (the freeze-adjust block closes at line 269). Ordering is correct for the scenario described: `applyWorksheetShift` runs `replaceMerges(...)` at line 598 and only then `shiftWorksheetViewState(...)` at line 611, so the snap observes the already-shifted merge map. The backend controller reaches it — packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:355 `applyShift` calls `applyWorksheetShift(...)`, and the controller doc at line 70 states "`shiftWorksheetViewState` then snaps the boundary past that block." The behavior is pinned by packages/sheets/test/workbook/worksheet-structure.test.ts:198-220, which asserts an insert that pushes the boundary 3→4 and merge A3:A5→A4:A6 results in frozenRows 6 (snapped), with a negative-case test at 222-237. Therefore an API insert/delete cannot leave a merge straddling the freeze via this path, and the premise of the finding (and its downstream 409 consequence) does not hold.
